title: The mission must prove, not expose
excerpts: Compact allows applications where users can prove facts about their data without revealing the data itself.
That promise is the foundation of programmable privacy in the mission.

title: Technical definition of a ZK proof
excerpts: A zero-knowledge proof lets one party prove a statement is true without revealing additional information beyond its validity.

title: Roles in the proof
excerpts: The book presents one side as the prover and the other as the verifier.
Validity travels; the secret does not.

title: Operational example from the book
excerpts: A ZK proof can verify that a user is over 21 without revealing the actual birth date.

title: The circuit is the mathematical engine
excerpts: The Compact compiler generates zero-knowledge circuits used to prove the correctness of ledger interactions.

title: What a circuit solves
excerpts: Circuits define business logic, generate proofs, and may be exposed to TypeScript.

title: Export for outside calls
excerpts: Use `export` to make circuits callable from TypeScript.

title: The proof is generated at runtime
excerpts: Real proofs are generated locally at runtime to enable selective disclosure.

title: A witness does not cross without permission
excerpts: Private information should be disclosed only when necessary.

title: What `disclose()` does
excerpts: `disclose()` explicitly declares the intention to use a witness-derived value in a context that might reveal it.

title: Disclosure as the exception
excerpts: Compact treats privacy as the default and disclosure as an explicit exception.

title: The exact line from the book
excerpts: The example moves a witness value into ledger with a single `disclose()` call.

title: The compiler tracks witness flow
excerpts: The compiler detects undeclared disclosures of witness data through a protection program.

title: What the alert means
excerpts: The error indicates that a potentially private value could be disclosed without an explicit declaration.

title: Disclosure may be indirect
excerpts: Disclosure is not always direct; the compiler follows the value through the program.

title: Privacy by default
excerpts: Privacy is the default and disclosure requires explicit intent.
